provenance.prompt:
Create one original transparent RGBA production sprite sheet for Reed Ashcroft's right-facing `dunk-tomahawk` action in JAMVERSE ’96.

Canvas and layout: exactly 15 different complete full-body drawings in five equal columns by three equal rows, strict left-to-right and top-to-bottom order, all on one 1619×971 transparent canvas. Place exactly one isolated Reed figure in each cell. Keep a consistent figure scale and stable foot baseline; gameplay supplies jump translation. Keep every braid tip, finger, shoe and dark outline safely inside its cell, with broad transparent gutters. No touching, clipping, overlap, fusion, duplicate drawings, mirrored copies, or pose crossing cell boundaries. True alpha-zero transparency outside each figure. Draw crisp, chunky, readable 1990s arcade pixel art with a near-black dark outline and consistent light from the upper left.

Character identity: Reed is a young adult human man with medium-brown skin, dark focused eyes and brows, a small dark goatee, and long dark purple-black braids gathered into a compact high topknot. Preserve his same recognizable face and natural athletic muscular human build in every view. Long braids remain attached to the scalp and move with his head; they are never a cape, scarf, or extra limb. He wears a blank Chicago Condas basketball uniform in deep purple with gold trim, white lower-leg wear and purple-and-gold basketball shoes. Keep natural human anatomy and hands with five fingers. No glasses, headband, armor, fantasy anatomy, text, numbers, symbols or logos.

Action: a forceful one-handed tomahawk dunk, clearly different from a two-handed power dunk or full-body spin. Reed already controls an invisible game ball in his right hand. He approaches facing screen right, plants, jumps, cocks the ball back above and behind his head with his right elbow bent, then drives the right arm forward and downward through an imaginary rim for the release. His left arm balances the movement. Keep the ball position and right hand readable without drawing the ball. The game renders the separate basketball and hoop; draw neither.

Exact pose sequence, one distinct drawing per cell:

0. Rightward approach with a compact athletic stride; eyes toward the imaginary rim; invisible ball secure in the right hand near the right hip.
1. Plant the lead foot, sink the hips and bring the ball up toward the right shoulder; left arm balances forward.
2. TAKEOFF: both feet leave the floor, torso rises, right hand carries the ball above shoulder height.
3. Early ascent: right elbow bends and draws the invisible ball high behind the head; one knee lifts and the other leg trails naturally.
4. Mid-ascent: shoulders coil slightly, right forearm is cocked behind the crown with the hand still gripping the invisible ball; left arm reaches forward for balance.
5. Strong tomahawk wind-up: right elbow is bent overhead, hand behind the crown; chest opens and knees gather.
6. Rise toward the apex with the right arm still cocked; the ball remains behind the head, clearly separated from the hair silhouette.
7. PEAK: highest body point, natural tucked knees, right elbow bent overhead in a powerful tomahawk position; left hand open for balance.
8. Begin the strike: rotate the shoulders toward the right-side rim and lift the cocked right elbow forward; keep the invisible ball in the right hand.
9. Pre-release: extend the right arm forward and slightly above the head, wrist cocked, body traveling toward the rim.
10. RELEASE: snap the right arm downward through the imaginary rim and open the right hand only now; Reed is empty-handed after release.
11. FINISH: right arm follows through down across the body, left arm extends for balance; show the empty right hand and continuing motion.
12. Descend, shoulders unwind to face screen right; both arms spread naturally to stabilize.
13. Landing approach: torso upright, knees unfold beneath him and arms remain out for balance.
14. LAND: both shoes meet the ground, knees bend deeply to absorb impact, and Reed settles into a balanced ready stance.

Every drawing must be a complete, independently articulated full-body Reed with the same face, goatee, attached braided topknot, uniform, white lower-leg wear and shoes. Make the tomahawk motion legible in a small game sprite. Do not move the whole sprite upward to fake the jump; keep feet on the shared baseline in the sheet. Do not put a ball in the art, even as a highlight, prop, shadow or effect. No hoop, rim, court, ground shadow, glow, background, border, cell guides, grid, text, effect, opponent, passer or prop. Return only the transparent sprite sheet.

provenance.sourcePrompt:
Generate an original six-frame action animation contact sheet for basketball, on transparent background, 3 columns by 2 rows, reading left to right then down. Athlete: Juniper Vale, based strictly on the attached canonical portrait and clean empty-hand gameplay sprite. She is a compact natural human athletic adult woman with light-warm skin, dark focused eyes, abundant dark-purple curls gathered high with one small gold tie, Chicago Condas purple-and-gold uniform, dark knee pads and matching shoes. Maintain her face, hair, body and colors across every frame. Right-facing three-quarter view, consistent game-sprite scale and camera.

There must be absolutely no basketball and no object in or near her hands in any pose. Do not show a sphere, circle, ball-like shape, prop or held item. Her hands are visibly empty with separated fingers and palms open. Pose sequence: (0) stable open-hand ready stance, arms relaxed near waist; (1) bring empty open hands toward mid-chest, palms facing each other but separated; (2) chest-pass load with elbows bent and empty hands open at chest sides, palms slightly forward; (3) pass-release anchor: one forward step with both empty arms extended straight at chest height and palms/fingers fully open; (4) empty-hand follow-through, arms forward and weight over lead foot; (5) recover to balanced ready stance. No ball in any of the six cells.

Each 512×512 cell contains one complete figure centered at uniform scale, maximum 68% cell height and 56% cell width; leave at least 15% clear transparent padding on all four sides. Separate figures with broad gutters. No clipping, crop, overlap, touch, or shadow. Background must be fully transparent RGBA, with no glow or gradient. The uniform front is plain purple fabric with gold trim only: no letters, numbers, badges, logos or text. No extra athletes, anatomy variants, fantasy traits, glasses, extra jewelry, checkerboard, floor, panels, borders or grid lines.

review.notes: Visually reviewed six separate complete Juniper poses on the transparent source. Light-warm skin, dark eyes, abundant dark-purple high curls with gold tie, compact natural build, kneepads and purple/gold Condas kit match runtime cell1. All six hands are empty; no basketball, jersey numeral or extra prop remains. The bottom-left drawing is the chest-pass release anchor. Eight-connected alpha segmentation at threshold64 identifies exactly six unique bodies in row-major order; each stays inside the source sheet and can be isolated without cutting neighboring pose pixels. Atlas packing uniformly scales and baseline-aligns original pixels only. Native Canvas standard and zoom120 previews show production art in both facings and place the separate ball at the frame3 release hand.

provenance.prompt: Create an original JAMVERSE '96 2D arcade basketball animation sheet for canonical captain Wicked. Use the portrait in the THIRD ROW, FOURTH COLUMN of the supplied seven-column roster portrait atlas as the face and hair identity guide; ignore all other portraits. Wicked is an adult gothic woman with long vivid crimson-red hair and two distinctive swept-back dark horns, a poised dangerous stylish expression and powerful controlled athletic build. Idle frames are subtly distinct standing variations. Ready/held-ball poses keep both hands empty because the game renders the ball separately. Dribble poses show varied right-handed low reaches, with dribble pose6 the lowest. Run poses have clear alternating stride. Dribble-run poses show a low run dribble, with pose7 the lowest reach. Every figure faces right in a consistent side three-quarter view. Feet, hair and horns are fully visible and comfortably inset from all image edges. No ball, props, words, numbers, cell borders, floor, court, shadows, glow, duplicate figure, or watermark.

Each figure is independently articulated, with obvious transparent gaps between neighbors and at least 8% transparent margin at both top and bottom. Figure height should stay below about 78% of the canvas height; keep antlers, flowing hair and bare feet comfortably away from all image borders. Character must face SCREEN-LEFT with body and stride, three-quarter view; never mirror a reference. Use reference image1 as precise face canon, reference image2 only for body scale, outfit, palette and sprite style. Adult male supernatural athlete with azure blue skin, messy icy-white hair, TWO small blue deer antlers, anatomical LEFT sclera black and RIGHT sclera white, both eyes with cyan irises and clearly open; no visor or eye band. Single smoky tilted black orbital ring around mouth/chin BELOW both eyes, exactly like the face reference, never across eyes. Bare upper chest with a clear golden hollow outline heart. Ripped gray jeans, bare feet, no shoes, no armor. Preserve anatomical eye sides even though body faces screen-left; draw the eye geometry anatomically, not by flipping. Empty hands; physics ball added by game. Crisp readable original late-1990s arcade art with bold dark ink lines, consistent face/body/outfit, complete figure. Transparent RGBA only: no checkerboard, no floor, court, shadows, glow, text, labels, numbers, panels, cell lines, logos, ball, or extra props. Exactly seven separate poses in one row. Strip1 poses, seven different moments read left to right: idle frame1 neutral relaxed stance; idle2 gentle inhale, shoulders slightly raised; idle3 weight shifts onto left foot; idle4 subtle weight shift onto right foot; idle5 one heel lifts and settles; idle6 relaxed arm and torso variation; idle-with-ball frame1, a slightly lower ready stance with empty hands cupped to receive a separate game ball. All upright, distinct, naturally continuous.

provenance.prompt: Six independently generated left-facing seven-pose strips. Their complete prompts and source hashes are in tools/generate-art/e-indigo-locomotion-left-strips.json.

review.source: The six source strips were visually reviewed; the assembled atlas passed exact42 body separation, margins, transparent RGBA and 7x6 reading-order checks. Pending final packed-atlas review.

assembly.operation: Each strip's seven existing alpha components were isolated by nearest-component ownership after transparent16px outer padding. Crops were uniformly scaled to a common maximum height174px and placed on a transparent192x192 grid at a shared baseline184. No poses were drawn, duplicated or mirrored.
